decision: REVISE DESIGN BEFORE HTTP IMPLEMENTATION: MAKE COMPLETED-ROOT RELEASE GATE EXPLICIT
review_scope: Bounded deferred-send boundary refinement only; no implementation source re-audit
positive_assessment: Defer the same original postcommit closure until after session save/RequestHandled, preserving its context/identity/reader/metadata admission and original ten-second deadline.
Mint only after positive original framework commit/proof; no idle-PDO inference, recapture, new lifetime or read-only frame across session writes.
Keep provisional bytes private, materialize supported headers/cookies before the final proof, preserve non-HTTP immediate closure and original-only frame cleanup.
Actual sent response status/body must be tested; unsent TestResponse is not release evidence.

required_design_clarification.title: Calling send is not itself proof that all root callbacks have finished
required_design_clarification.evidence: Installed Kernel.handle dispatches RequestHandled before returning; an ordinary listener can invoke its response.send while later listeners remain. Symfony also exposes sendHeaders/sendContent/__toString independently. The current draft names real send but does not specify a trusted completed-root phase or premature-entry refusal.
required_design_clarification.requirement: Specify a trusted completed-root release phase, or reject emission while the original root/middleware/RequestHandled callback execution remains active. All public emission entry points must share the one-use original boundary; premature/reentrant/second private release must not emit headers or prepared bytes. Refuse private release if headers were already sent. No caller-authored flag, new authority/deadline or arbitrary fallback source may substitute.
required_controls: Real RequestHandled early-send listener followed by a later scope/mount withdrawal: no premature private output; actual final send refuses.
Direct sendHeaders/sendContent/stringification before authorized final release exposes no prepared bytes/headers.
Reentrant and second-send/failed-send lifecycle, plus headers-already-sent refusal and unused boundary cleanup.
Ordinary actual post-kernel send with genuine session save remains positive.
